sections.h2: Which county tax office bills a Round Rock house?
sections.html:
Your bill comes from either the Williamson County or the Travis County tax office, according to where your parcel is located. Round Rock sits in both counties, and its finance page says the city contracts with both offices to collect its levy.

Official contacts, from the city's finance page:

  • Williamson County Tax Office, 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, 512-943-1601.
  • Travis County Tax Office, 2433 Ridgepoint Dr., Austin, 512-854-9473.
  • Williamson Central Appraisal District, 625 F.M. 1460, Georgetown, 512-930-3787.
  • Travis Central Appraisal District, 850 E Anderson Lane, Austin, 512-834-9317.

Each county runs a lookup site where an address shows what every unit on that parcel charges. Confirm the county before you phone, since each office holds its own accounts.

sections.h2: How much is the Round Rock city levy?
sections.html:
The city adopted 37.2000 cents on each $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2025-2026. Its page also shows a median home worth $395,240 on the 2025 rolls and an estimated city tax bill of $1,470 for that median home.

Treat that as one line of a longer statement. Other taxing units stack their own lines on the same bill, so the city figure alone understates your total. The page adds that proposed rates are published every year under Tax Code Section 26.04, and that delinquency begins February 1.

sections.h2: When does a Round Rock tax bill go late?
sections.html:
Statements land in October, and January 31 is the last clean day. On February 1 the account turns delinquent, with a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest, and by July 1 the penalty alone has reached 12 percent. A collection lawyer's fee of up to 20 percent can follow.

A split plan lets you pay half by November 30 and half by June 30, and owners who are 65-plus or disabled can use four installments. The Comptroller's payment page also explains penalty waivers and homestead payment plans of up to 36 months.

sections.h2: How do exemptions and caps lower a Round Rock tax bill?
sections.html:
The largest lever is the homestead exemption: $140,000 comes off the value school districts tax, and a person who is 65-plus or disabled gets $60,000 more. A city or county may layer on a percentage exemption of up to 20 percent, so ask each office what it chose.

  • Appraised value on a homestead may rise no more than 10 percent a year once the first qualifying January 1 has passed.
  • A school tax freeze holds a senior's school bill at the amount set in the year they qualified.
  • Disabled veterans can get a partial exemption tied to a VA rating, or a total one at 100 percent.
  • File applications with the appraisal district by April 30, using forms listed on the Comptroller's exemption page.

Census figures show 11.2 percent of residents at 65 or older and 6,913 veterans, so these breaks matter locally. If you buy after January 1 and the seller never claimed the exemption, you can claim it right away.

sections.h2: How do I contest my Round Rock appraised value?
sections.html:
Deliver a written protest to the appraisal review board by May 15, or by day 30 after your notice arrived if that is later. Homestead notices begin around April 1.

A board ruling you dislike can go to district court, arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the value is over $1,000,000. Pay the undisputed part of the tax before the delinquency date to protect the appeal. Ask the district early for your property record card and its comparable sales.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show about Round Rock?
sections.html:
Round Rock's population rose 18.2% from the April 2020 base to the July 2025 estimate. The city has 48,647 households of 2.61 people on average, with median income of $99,287.

  • Owners paying a mortgage spend a median $2,364 a month, against $925 for owners with none.
  • The average commute runs 24.9 minutes.
  • Bachelor's degrees or more are held by 44.8% of adults 25 and up.
  • Land area is 37.64 square miles, with 3,174 residents per square mile in 2020.

A citywide median hides street-level gaps, so weigh your house against recent sales in your subdivision.

sections.h2: Which parts of Round Rock's past matter to a house sale?
sections.html:
The first settlement stood by a natural ford on Brushy Creek, near the round rock that gave the town its name, and the post office was renamed Round Rock in 1854 because another community already used Brushy. The railroad era created a second, newer downtown in 1876, and a first zoning ordinance followed in 1969.

Water has been both a limit and a hazard. A prolonged drought in 1978 dried up local wells, and in 1981 a 30-inch line from Lake Georgetown secured the supply. Flash floods from Tropical Storm Hermine on September 8, 2010 forced evacuations near Lake Creek and flooded 44 homes, mostly in Round Rock West and on Lake Creek Circle. Voters in the Brushy Creek Water Control and Improvement District approved a small property tax in 2002 to maintain flood control dams, which is the kind of district charge worth finding on your own bill.

Dell's 1994 move of its world headquarters to the city brought, in the city's words, a significant jump in the tax base. Hospitals, a Texas State nursing campus and Austin Community College followed through 2010.

sections.h2: Do Round Rock short-term rentals owe their own tax?
sections.html:
They do. Under the city's hotel occupancy FAQ, a rental of fewer than 30 consecutive days is short-term, and it carries 9 percent of monthly net receipts, built from a 7 percent hotel tax and a 2 percent venue tax.

  • Registration is $35 at first and $25 to renew before January 1.
  • Each property registers separately.
  • A return is filed monthly, including empty months, no later than the final day of the next month.
  • Penalties run 5, 10 or 15 percent by lateness, with 10 percent interest from day 61.
  • The city notes that Airbnb and Vrbo do not remit this tax on your behalf.

Before selling a house that was rented, file every open return and submit the closure form.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Round Rock tax at a sale?
sections.html:
Each year's tax lien forms on January 1 and rides with the house. A buyer cannot get clean title until delinquent balances are cleared, and the January 1 owner remains answerable for that year even after the transfer.

Your escrow officer settles the account from the buyer's funds at the closing table, so get a written payoff from the right county, including any special district balance. The county clerk records the deed, and the state's clerk manual lists $5.00 for page one plus $4.00 per added page.

faqs.q: What per-$100 rate does Round Rock charge?
faqs.a: The city's adopted figure is 37.2000 cents per $100 for fiscal year 2025-2026. Counties, school districts and special districts levy theirs separately.

faqs.q: Williamson County or Travis County: which gets my payment?
faqs.a: Pay the county that contains your parcel. The city contracts with both offices, and each property falls under only one. A lookup by address settles it.

faqs.q: What if I miss the January 31 date?
faqs.a: It is delinquent on February 1, with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest added at once. The penalty reaches 12 percent by July 1, and interest keeps accruing.

faqs.q: Is hotel tax due on an Airbnb in Round Rock?
faqs.a: Yes. Stays under 30 days owe 9 percent of net receipts, split 7 and 2 between the hotel and venue taxes. You register each property and file monthly.

faqs.q: Can a Round Rock house with back taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is cleared at the closing table. Request the payoff in writing from the correct county so you know your net before accepting an offer.
